title: Habakkuk
lead: Habakkuk is a prophet of Judah in the years when Babylon rose (about 609-597 BC) and the book that bears his name: a conversation in which he complains to God about violence, hears that the Chaldeans are coming, argues again, waits at his watch, receives the vision that the righteous will live by faithfulness, and ends with a prayer-psalm of the LORD's coming and a vow of joy.

sections.b: Habakkuk is named only in his own book. Later tradition adds a tribe and a hometown (the Lives of the Prophets) and a flight by angel to Babylon (Bel and the Dragon, in the Greek Daniel). The book is quoted in the New Testament at Acts 13:41 (1:5), Romans 1:17 and Galatians 3:11 (2:4) and Hebrews 10:37-38 (2:3-4), and echoed at Luke 1:47 (3:18). A scroll from Qumran, the Habakkuk Pesher, comments on chapters 1 and 2. The Talmud finds the center of the commandments in 2:4 (Makkot 24a).
